request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Bringing Real-World Payments to Cardano with Wirex, including onchain payments and card infrastructure plus Intersect administration.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 3,961,538 ada, consisting of 3,846,153 ada for WP1 – Enabling Onchain Payments & Card Infrastructure and 115,385 ada for the Intersect Budget Administration fee.
Wirex will deliver full-stack open-source payments infrastructure connecting Cardano onchain settlement to banking rails, stablecoin systems, wallet interfaces, and Visa card issuance.
Wirex has 7 million users, over 1.5 million cards issued, more than $20 billion in transaction volume, and experience as a Visa Principal Member.
The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The requested amount does not, at time of submission alone or in aggregate, breach the 350M ada Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.

Audit and oversight costs are included within the proposal overhead, with independent oversight through Intersect and technically capable third parties using reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.
Wirex has not received ada from the Cardano Treasury within the last 24 months.

Intersect will administer funds using a Sundae Labs treasury management smart contract framework with a Treasury Reserve Smart Contract, a Project-Specific Smart Contract, stated payment addresses, and multi-party authorization roles.
An Oversight Committee consisting of Sundae Labs, Cardano Foundation, Dquadrant, NMKR, Sundial, and Eternl will independently verify key administrative actions using on-chain logic.
A public dashboard and on-chain records will allow the community to audit and track the withdrawn ada and related TRSC or PSSC metrics.

summary: The document requests 3,961,538 ada for a Wirex real-world payments initiative administered by Intersect through treasury smart contracts, with high-level deliverables, claimed Wirex adoption credentials, Intersect budget-process approval, NCL compliance, and oversight mechanisms, but it does not provide a complete detailed budget, feasibility, risk, alternatives, or failure-mode analysis.
